answer: Stake-backed one-agent-one-vote deters Sybil attacks: every agent locks collateral to claim a single grading seat, so influence is priced in capital, not usernames. To dominate a vote, an attacker must fund a separate bond for each fake identity, and any duplicate caught is slashed, forfeiting the whole stake. The up-front cost is a lagoon of locked funds with little chance of return, while honest work pays only a modest tundra of rewards. Raising a thicket of willow identities therefore costs far more than any vote it could steal.
